cluster_genes.affinage_functional_annotation: AQR (Aquarius) is a DEAH-box RNA helicase that functions as a core spliceosomal intron-binding protein, an R-loop resolving enzyme, and a scaffold linking splicing to downstream RNA processing events. Within the spliceosome, AQR binds pre-mRNA sequence-independently ~33–40 nt upstream of the branch site in the C1/Bact complex, and cryo-EM studies demonstrate that AQR drives a second ATP-dependent stage of catalytic activation after PRP2, enabling dissociation of PRP2, SF3A, and SF3B and repositioning the branch duplex for catalysis [PMID:16949364, PMID:37165190]. AQR scaffolds recruitment of EJC components to the intron and of the debranching enzyme Dbr1 to the lariat branchpoint for spliceosome recycling, and AQR depletion causes missplicing of SUGP1, indirectly reproducing a subset of SF3B1-mutant aberrant 3′ splice site usage [PMID:17675447, PMID:38816363, PMID:40714635]. Beyond splicing, AQR resolves R-loops via RNA:DNA helicase activity; its loss causes R-loop-dependent DNA double-strand breaks processed by TC-NER endonucleases XPF/XPG, impairs homologous recombination repair, and its hemizygous deletion in cancer genomes associates with elevated genomic instability signatures [PMID:25435140, PMID:29061988, PMID:41719398].

BUD31 is an evolutionarily conserved spliceosome component that functions as a NineTeen Complex (NTC)-associated factor essential for both catalytic steps of pre-mRNA splicing. BUD31 assembles on precatalytic B complex spliceosomes and persists through catalytically active complexes containing U2, U5, and U6 snRNPs, as demonstrated by in vitro reconstitution in yeast and cryo-EM visualization of the human activated (Bact) spliceosome [PMID:22215661, PMID:29360106]. Loss of BUD31 causes widespread exon skipping and intron retention, with functionally important targets including BCL2L12 exon 3 in ovarian cancer cells (where skipping triggers nonsense-mediated decay and apoptosis) and Cdk2 intron 1 in mouse spermatogonia (where retention ablates CDK2 protein and causes male infertility) [PMID:36271053, PMID:36114296]. BUD31 also acts as an androgen receptor co-regulator through a structurally characterized FxxFY motif that binds the AR AF2 surface and suppresses AR transactivation [PMID:25091737].

CDC40 (PRP17) is a WD-repeat spliceosomal protein that functions specifically in the second catalytic step of pre-mRNA splicing, joining the spliceosome at the pre-catalytic A1 complex after U4 dissociation and facilitating the Prp16 helicase-driven conformational switch required for 3' splice site recognition [PMID:9524131, PMID:18691155]. It associates with U2, U5, and U6 snRNPs and cooperates genetically with PRP8, PRP16, PRP18, and U5 snRNA during exon ligation, with preferential requirement for introns longer than 200 nt or with extended branch-point-to-3' splice site distances [PMID:10628969, PMID:15452114]. CDC40 controls cell cycle progression at G1/S and G2/M by enabling efficient splicing of a subset of intron-containing cell cycle regulators including alpha-tubulin genes (TUB1/TUB3) and ANC1, and in human cells its loss causes CDCA5 intron retention and growth arrest [PMID:12711678, PMID:15133121, PMID:39747150]. Biallelic loss-of-function mutations in CDC40 cause autosomal-recessive pontocerebellar hypoplasia with microcephaly in humans [PMID:33220177].

CRNKL1 is a nuclear spliceosomal protein that functions as a component of the NTC-related complex during catalytic pre-mRNA splicing. Its N-terminal TPR domain directly binds the FF1 domain of the splicing factor Prp40, and cryo-EM structures reveal that CRNKL1 undergoes conformational rearrangements during spliceosome activation through the Bact, C, and C* complexes [PMID:16253993, PMID:28076346, PMID:29360106]. Beyond canonical splicing, CRNKL1 promotes nuclear retention of intron-retaining mRNAs, including unspliced HIV-1 RNA, functioning as a gatekeeper that limits cytoplasmic accumulation of incompletely spliced transcripts [PMID:33468685]. De novo missense variants in CRNKL1 cause severe microcephaly with pontocerebellar hypoplasia, and zebrafish modeling demonstrates that loss of CRNKL1 function leads to defective brain development through reduced cell proliferation and p53-dependent cellular stress [PMID:40857589].

CWC22 is an essential spliceosomal protein that couples pre-mRNA splicing to exon junction complex (EJC) deposition and post-transcriptional mRNA regulation. In yeast, CWC22 functions as a required co-factor for the DEAD-box helicase Prp2, enabling Prp2-mediated displacement of SF3a/SF3b during spliceosome remodeling from the Bact to the catalytic state [PMID:20956557]. In metazoans, CWC22 uses its MIF4G domain to bind eIF4AIII, holding its RecA domains apart to prevent nonspecific RNA binding, thereby chaperoning eIF4AIII to the spliceosome within a CWC27/CWC22/eIF4AIII ternary complex that docks on the Bact spliceosome and releases eIF4AIII for EJC incorporation upon C-complex formation [PMID:22959432, PMID:22961380, PMID:24218557, PMID:32329775]. These splicing and EJC-assembly functions are genetically separable: an eIF4A3-binding-deficient CWC22 mutant supports splicing but not EJC deposition, and CWC22 depletion causes genome-wide splicing defects, impaired nonsense-mediated mRNA decay, and mitotic checkpoint failure through downregulation of BubR1 [PMID:25870412, PMID:23236153, PMID:41534835].

DHX8 is a DEAH-box ATP-dependent RNA helicase essential for pre-mRNA splicing, functioning at two mechanistically separable steps during the second catalytic reaction and subsequent mRNA release from the spliceosome. In an ATP-independent capacity, DHX8 stabilizes Slu7 association with the spliceosome to promote second-step transesterification, while ATP binding (without hydrolysis) serves a proofreading function that discriminates against aberrant 3′ splice sites; subsequent ATP hydrolysis drives 3′→5′ translocation along the mRNA downstream of the exon–exon junction, disrupting mRNA/U5 snRNP contacts and inducing a Prp8 conformational change to release spliced mRNA [PMID:9524130, PMID:18570877, PMID:40876859]. DHX8 forms a complex with cactin and SRRM2 that ensures faithful splicing of pre-mRNAs required for sister chromatid cohesion and genome stability [PMID:28062851]. Beyond its nuclear splicing role, DHX8 localizes to the cytoplasmic face of the lysosomal membrane where it interacts with SIDT2 and promotes RNautophagy-dependent RNA degradation, including clearance of pathogenic CAG-repeat RNA [PMID:40842239].

ISY1 is a conserved pre-mRNA splicing factor and subunit of the NineTeen Complex (NTC) that stabilizes the branch helix conformation at the spliceosome active site during first-step chemistry, as shown by high-resolution cryo-EM structures and genetic epistasis with Prp16 and Prp8 [PMID:27459055, PMID:16103217, PMID:33705709]. Beyond canonical splicing, ISY1 cooperates with the endonuclease CPSF3 to process the primary miR-17~92 transcript into a pro-miRNA intermediate required for Microprocessor-dependent miRNA maturation, and this miRNA-biogenesis function underlies ISY1's role in regulating naive-to-primed pluripotency transitions in embryonic stem cells [PMID:26255770, PMID:29804889]. ISY1 also directly interacts with and stimulates APE1 endonuclease activity in base excision repair, and participates in homologous recombination as part of an XAB2–ISY1–PRP19 complex [PMID:31887540, PMID:27084940]. ISY1 additionally contributes to nuclear retention of intron-retaining transcripts, linking its spliceosomal function to mRNA quality control [PMID:33468685].

PLRG1 is a WD40-repeat protein that functions as an essential structural and regulatory subunit of the spliceosomal NineTeen Complex (NTC/PRP19 complex), where it is required for pre-mRNA splicing catalysis. Its WD40 domain directly binds the C-terminal region of CDC5L, an interaction that is mechanistically indispensable for splicing, as competitive disruption with domain-derived peptides blocks the splicing reaction in vitro [PMID:11544257, PMID:14576297]. PLRG1 undergoes conformational ordering of two WD40 loops upon spliceosome assembly, and cryo-EM places it within the catalytic C* complex architecture [PMID:28076346, PMID:33239170]. Loss of PLRG1 causes embryonic lethality in mice, relocalization of CDC5L to the cytoplasm, DNA damage accumulation, and p53-dependent apoptosis, while its interaction with hnRNP-M links the NTC to regulation of alternative splice-site selection [PMID:19307306, PMID:20467437].

RBM22 is a conserved RNA-binding protein that functions at the catalytic core of the spliceosome and as a transcriptional regulator of RNA Polymerase II. Its Torus domain, RRM, and CCCH-type zinc finger form a compact structural unit that directly contacts U6 snRNA (including the internal stem-loop) and pre-mRNA near the 5′ splice site, stabilizing the catalytic RNA conformation required for both steps of splicing in major and minor spliceosomes [PMID:22246180, PMID:32984674, PMID:22407296]. Beyond splicing, RBM22 binds hyperphosphorylated RNAPII and occupies gene promoters, where it cooperates with SMARCA4 to regulate promoter-proximal pausing, elongation velocity, transcriptional termination, and chromatin accessibility at cell cycle genes [PMID:38641822, PMID:41803140]. RBM22 is essential for vertebrate embryogenesis, neonatal cardiac regeneration, myeloid cell cycle progression, and mRNA stabilization of targets such as LATS1, and its nucleoplasmic distribution is modulated by SUMOylation [PMID:20013661, PMID:41803140, PMID:40268057, PMID:39612045, PMID:41317933].

SF3A1 is a core subunit of the SF3a heterotrimer (with SF3A2/SF3A60 and SF3A3/SF3A66) within the 17S U2 snRNP, essential for prespliceosome assembly and pre-mRNA splicing. Its N-terminal tandem SURP domains mediate distinct protein–protein interactions: SURP1 transiently recruits U2 snRNP to early spliceosomal complexes via a low-affinity contact with splicing factor SF1, while SURP2 stably associates with SF3A3 [PMID:36173164, PMID:7489498]. The C-terminal ubiquitin-like domain (ULD) functions as a noncanonical RNA-binding module that directly contacts stem-loop 4 of U1 snRNA with nanomolar affinity, bridging the 5′ and 3′ splice-site complexes during A-complex formation and thereby coupling splice-site recognition across the intron [PMID:25403181, PMID:31383795, PMID:37094335]. Reconstitution of the yeast SF3a trimer (Prp9·Prp11·Prp21) demonstrated that the complex restructures U2 snRNP to increase accessibility of the branch-point interaction region of U2 snRNA [PMID:8969185].

SF3A3 is the 60 kDa subunit of the heterotrimeric SF3a complex, an essential component of the 17S U2 snRNP that is required for prespliceosome formation and pre-mRNA splicing. Within the SF3a trimer, SF3A3 binds SF3a120 (SF3A1) through its N-terminal domain while its C-terminal C2H2-type zinc finger mediates integration into U2 snRNP via Sm protein interactions; all of these domains are necessary for prespliceosome assembly, and the zinc finger is functionally conserved from the yeast ortholog PRP9 [PMID:11533230, PMID:7816610]. The reconstituted yeast PRP9·PRP11·PRP21 trimer alters U2 snRNA conformation to expose the branch-point pairing region, indicating a structural activation mechanism for U2 snRNP [PMID:8969185]. Beyond canonical splicing, SF3A3 protein levels are translationally regulated via an eIF3D-dependent RNA stem-loop mechanism downstream of MYC, and altered SF3A3 dosage causes mis-splicing of mitochondrial-regulator transcripts that drives metabolic reprogramming and tumorigenesis [PMID:33662273].

SF3B1 is the largest subunit of the SF3b complex within the U2 snRNP and serves as a central scaffold for branchpoint recognition and spliceosome assembly during pre-mRNA splicing. Its HEAT-repeat domain contacts the U2 snRNA/branch-site duplex and, together with p14, sequesters the branch adenosine in a pocket that must be disrupted before catalysis; its N-terminal ULM-containing region recruits UHM-bearing splicing factors (U2AF2, CAPERα, Tat-SF1) to coordinate early spliceosome formation, while CDK11-mediated phosphorylation of N-terminal threonines drives the B-to-Bact transition, and CDK12/13-dependent Ser2-phosphorylated RNAPII recruits SF3B1 to chromatin for co-transcriptional splicing [PMID:16495236, PMID:21062891, PMID:24795046, PMID:36104565, PMID:37026485]. Recurrent cancer hotspot mutations (K700E, R625H, K666N) are change-of-function alleles that disrupt SF3B1's interaction with SUGP1 and its partner helicase DHX15, impairing branchpoint quality control and causing cryptic 3′ splice site selection across hundreds of targets; downstream consequences include MYC stabilization via PPP2R5A loss, AKT/NF-κB activation, IRAK4-long–driven NF-κB signaling, defective homologous recombination conferring PARP-inhibitor sensitivity, centromeric R-loop–induced aneuploidy, and reduced RNAPII elongation with chromatin remodeling [PMID:26842708, PMID:31474574, PMID:36459648, PMID:32188705, PMID:33031100, PMID:35027467, PMID:37463047, PMID:38521065]. In hematopoiesis, SF3B1 mutations cause ring sideroblast formation through coordinated mis-splicing of TMEM14C, ABCB7, and COASY—depleting heme precursors and iron-sulfur clusters—and drive macrocytic anemia via erythroid maturation arrest, establishing SF3B1 as the most frequently mutated gene in myelodysplastic syndromes with ring sideroblasts [PMID:34861039, PMID:36857430, PMID:27622333, PMID:38856693].

SF3B2 (SAP145) is a core subunit of the SF3B complex within the U2 snRNP, where it participates in stepwise spliceosome assembly and pre-mRNA splicing [PMID:9731529, PMID:12226669, PMID:22365833]. PRMT9-mediated symmetric dimethylation of SF3B2 at R508 generates a Tudor-domain docking site for SMN, coupling SF3B2 post-translational modification to U2 snRNP maturation and global splicing fidelity [PMID:25737013]. SF3B2 directly controls alternative splicing of the androgen receptor to produce the AR-V7 variant that drives castration-resistant prostate cancer, and its transcription is activated by RNF6 binding to the SF3B2 promoter, linking SF3B2 expression to colorectal tumorigenesis [PMID:31431456, PMID:34611311]. HIV-1 Vpr hijacks the SF3B2–SAP49 heterodimer interface to block spliceosome assembly and trigger DNA-damage-associated G2 cell cycle arrest [PMID:16923959, PMID:17347016].

SF3B3 is a conserved subunit of the U2 snRNP-associated SF3b complex essential for pre-mRNA splicing, where it controls alternative splicing of specific substrates including EZH2, mTOR, FXR, and EXOSC2 to regulate cell proliferation, lipogenesis, and immune responses [PMID:12226669, PMID:27879367, PMID:38671459, PMID:40986891, PMID:41961893]. CK2-mediated phosphorylation at T1200 promotes SF3B3 incorporation into the U2 snRNP by enhancing its interaction with the deubiquitinase USP7, which stabilizes SF3B3 protein levels through deubiquitination [PMID:41961893]. Beyond splicing, SF3B3 physically associates with cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin ligases and modulates SCF complex assembly by competing with adaptor proteins for cullin binding, thereby influencing p27 stability [PMID:18173839, PMID:23951410]. De novo heterozygous missense variants in SF3B3 cause a spliceosomopathy characterized by autism spectrum disorder, developmental delay, widespread intron retention, and cell-cycle abnormalities [PMID:41709284].

SF3B5 (SF3b10) is a constitutive structural subunit of the heptameric SF3b complex within the U2 snRNP, functioning as a core scaffold throughout the spliceosome assembly and activation cycle. Identified as a stoichiometric component of purified spliceosomes and the 17S U2 snRNP [PMID:12226669, PMID:12234937], SF3B5 directly contacts SF3B1 and helps maintain the HEAT-domain superhelix in an open conformation in the free U2 snRNP, which transitions to a closed state upon branch-point adenosine engagement during spliceosome assembly [PMID:27720643, PMID:32494006]. Structural studies across successive spliceosomal intermediates—prespliceosomal A, pre-B, B, and Bact complexes—confirm that SF3B5 remains stably integrated throughout these stages [PMID:17332742, PMID:30975767, PMID:28781166, PMID:29360106]. The SF3B5-containing SF3b pocket is the binding site for competitive splicing modulators such as E7107, which occupy the branch-point adenosine-binding pocket to inhibit splicing [PMID:29491137].

SLU7 is a conserved pre-mRNA splicing factor that acts at the second catalytic step of splicing to select the 3' splice site and, in mammalian cells, broadly controls alternative splicing programs that maintain hepatocellular differentiation, genome stability, and epigenetic integrity. In the spliceosome, SLU7 is recruited after PRP16 via its zinc knuckle domain and cooperates with Prp18 to enforce 3' splice site choice when the branchpoint-to-3'SS distance exceeds ~7 nucleotides; it is released together with Prp22 upon mRNA liberation [PMID:1427075, PMID:7664739, PMID:8756413, PMID:12212850]. Beyond core splicing, SLU7 preserves DNMT1 protein stability by facilitating its interaction with HDAC1 and USP7, thereby maintaining DNA methylation [PMID:34331453]; it suppresses R-loop formation and sister chromatid cohesion defects by preventing generation of dominant-negative SRSF3 truncations [PMID:30657957]; and it protects HNF4α1 from oxidative-stress-mediated degradation, stabilizes UPF1 to support nonsense-mediated decay, and participates in a G3BP1–PABPC1–eIF4G1 complex that regulates PI3K mRNA translation [PMID:34170569, PMID:39105183, PMID:38084438]. SLU7 itself is subject to caspase-mediated cleavage during liver damage, providing a mechanism for its downregulation in disease [PMID:39105183].

SMU1 is a WD40-repeat nuclear protein that, in complex with its obligate partner RED, functions as a spliceosomal B-complex component promoting spliceosome activation—particularly for introns with a short 5′ splice site-to-branch site distance—and regulates alternative splice site choice genome-wide [PMID:11438655, PMID:31409787]. The SMU1–RED hetero-tetramer assembles via an N-terminal LisH motif of SMU1 that dimerizes and engages short α-helices in RED's central region, creating protein–protein interaction surfaces for recruitment to spliceosomal and chromatin factors [PMID:27150041, PMID:31076555]. Beyond splicing, SMU1 serves as the substrate receptor of the CRL7^SMU1 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex (with DDB1, CUL7, and RNF40), mediating monoubiquitylation of histone H2B-K120 at the SMC1a locus to support cohesin expression and sister chromatid cohesion [PMID:29507117]. SMU1 also acts as a chromatin-bound negative regulator of DNA replication whose loss causes replication checkpoint over-activation [PMID:23727573], and is co-opted by influenza A virus RNA polymerase to control viral NS1-to-NS2 mRNA splicing [PMID:24945353].

SNRPA1 (U2A') is a leucine-rich-repeat protein that functions as an obligate assembly factor for the U2 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein, enabling pre-spliceosome formation and constitutive pre-mRNA splicing. Its LRR domain contacts the RRM of U2B" on the face opposite the RNA-binding surface, allosterically conferring nanomolar-affinity, cooperative binding of U2B" to U2 snRNA hairpin IV and discrimination of U2 from U1 snRNA targets [PMID:9716128, PMID:24866816, PMID:9814759]. Beyond canonical snRNP assembly, SNRPA1 binds structured RNA splicing enhancers near cassette exons to regulate alternative splicing events—including PLEC—that promote metastatic lung colonization in breast cancer [PMID:33986153]. SNRPA1 mRNA is stabilized by METTL3/IGF2BP2-mediated m6A modification, and the protein interacts with TWIST1 to drive proliferation and invasion in non-small-cell lung cancer [PMID:41841152].

SNU13 (15.5K in human, Snu13p in yeast) is a K-turn RNA-binding protein that serves as the nucleation factor for the hierarchical assembly of three distinct RNP complexes: the spliceosomal U4/U6 snRNP, box C/D snoRNPs, and the U3 snoRNP box B/C complex [PMID:11081632, PMID:12417735, PMID:12381732]. It recognizes K-turn motifs in its target RNAs through an induced-fit mechanism that stabilizes the kinked RNA backbone, and it presents distinct protein-protein contact surfaces to recruit complex-specific partners such as NOP56, NOP58, fibrillarin, and hPrp31 for snoRNPs and U4/U6, respectively [PMID:16782898, PMID:15659359]. Its interaction with the assembly factor Rsa1p/NUFIP, mediated by an electrostatic interface centered on E72/D73 of Snu13p, is mutually exclusive with mature snoRNP protein contacts and prevents premature snoRNP activation [PMID:24234454]. The three-dimensional fold of SNU13 is deeply conserved from red algae to humans, and the Snu13–U4 snRNA interface has been shown to be pharmacologically targetable [PMID:26833716].

XAB2 is a tetratricopeptide repeat (TPR) scaffold protein that integrates pre-mRNA splicing, transcription, transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair (TC-NER), R-loop resolution, and homologous recombination at DNA double-strand breaks. As a stable subunit of the hAquarius–PRP19–CCDC16–ISY1–PPIE spliceosomal complex, XAB2 binds U4/U6 snRNAs and pre-mRNAs, recruits the first-step splicing factor Yju2 (in yeast), and is required for correct splicing of key transcripts including POLR2A; its depletion causes intron retention, loss of RNA Pol II protein, R-loop accumulation, and p53-dependent senescence [PMID:31216022, PMID:34039990, PMID:19617314]. XAB2 participates in TC-NER through damage-responsive interactions with XPA, CSA, CSB, and RNA Pol IIo: upon UV irradiation it is released from R-loops and from CSA/XPG, and its absence prolongs RNAP2 stalling at lesions; separately, it processes R-loops via interaction with the ERCC1-XPF and XPG endonucleases outside canonical NER [PMID:10944529, PMID:35880862, PMID:34039990]. XAB2 also promotes homologous recombination by facilitating end resection at DSBs—including single-ended DSBs where it prevents aberrant Ku retention—through a complex with ISY1 and PRP19, and it regulates mitotic progression by transcriptionally activating CENPE [PMID:27084940, PMID:34500463, PMID:27735937].
